# In-cluster Nix binary cache

This directory is the clone-free bootstrap payload for Nagare's optional Attic
binary cache. A cloud context enables it with `NAGARE_NIX_CACHE_ENABLED=1` and
owns one GCS bucket, one HMAC credential, one managed PostgreSQL database, and
the workloads in `nagare-system`. Consumers opt in by mounting ConfigMap
`nagare-nix-cache-client` key `nix.conf` in `personal`.

The reviewed Attic source is commit
`12cbeca141f46e1ade76728bce8adc447f2166c6`, committed at
`2025-09-24T06:59:48-04:00`. Its official GHCR multi-architecture manifest is
`sha256:18574aba70fc89d2b695273fbe2e7b2f8ad7e8e786b4cc535124fbe14bada1d0`;
Nagare packages the Linux/amd64 manifest
`sha256:317924e10e70416e69d401880bb71b3aae69b413ecafcfc54018f61929464526`.
`nix/attic.nix` is the executable pin and the immutable payload adds
`attic-pin.json` plus `attic-server-image.tar.gz` here.

Run `nagare nix-cache-secret-init` once after applying the enabled Pulumi plan.
It writes only sops ciphertext to the context-owned secrets directory. Then run
`nagare nix-cache-bootstrap`; normal cloud `cluster-bootstrap` does this
automatically when enabled. `nagare nix-cache-status` reports the public
configuration without credentials.

Attic's S3 backend returns presigned GCS redirects for single-chunk NARs.
Opted-in clients therefore receive unrestricted TCP 443 egress in v1; Kubernetes
NetworkPolicy cannot constrain it to `storage.googleapis.com` by hostname. The
kube-router policy controller also has a short reconciliation window for newly
created Pods, so policy is defense in depth rather than a startup sandbox.

The JWT key authorizes Attic API tokens and lives only in operator-owned sops
ciphertext. The NAR signing key is generated by Attic and lives in PostgreSQL.
Rotating either key does not rotate the other. The GCS HMAC secret necessarily
passes through Pulumi state; its confidentiality is therefore the stack secrets
provider and state-bucket IAM boundary.
